rows.note: Use 想 as the all-purpose colloquial choice for wanting to do something, wishing for something, or wishing to meet someone.

example.english: I want to eat a bowl of fish-ball noodles.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 wun2 jyu4 daan6 fan2

rows.note: Use 要 when want means need, request, require, or be advised to do something.

example.english: I want to take today off because I have something to do.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 ngo5 jau5 si6 jiu3 cing2 gaa3

rows.note: Use 想要 to make the desire more explicit or stronger, especially when wanting a thing, an action, or someone sexually.

example.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 soeng2 jiu3 ni1 fan6 gung1

rows.note: Use 需要 as the all-purpose noun for something that is needed or necessary.

example.english: I'll tell you if I want anything.
example.jyutping: jau5 seoi1 jiu3 ngo5 zoi3 tung4 nei5 gong2

rows.note: Use 願望 when naming a personal wish or desire rather than a practical need.

example.english: Travelling around the world is my biggest want.
example.traditional: 環遊世界係我最大嘅願望。
example.jyutping: waan4 jau4 sai3 gaai3 hai6 ngo5 zeoi3 daai6 ge3 jyun6 mong6

rows.note: Use 缺乏 when referring to a deficiency or absence of something, especially in formal descriptions.

example.english: This region has long been affected by a want of drinking water.
example.traditional: 呢個地區長期缺乏食水。
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 dei6 keoi1 coeng4 kei4 kyut3 fat6 sik6 seoi2

rows.note: Use 貧窮 when referring to poverty or a state of having very little money or resources.

example.english: Living in want makes it hard for many families to get by.
example.traditional: 貧窮令好多家庭好難維持生計。
example.jyutping: pan4 kung4 ling6 hou2 do1 gaa1 ting4 hou2 naan4 wai4 ci4 saang1 gai3

rows.note: Use 愛 only for wanting someone out of romantic love, not for ordinary wanting or blunt sexual lust.

example.english: I love you and want to date you.
example.jyutping: ngo5 oi3 nei5 soeng2 tung4 nei5 paak3 to1
